title: GPU Fleet Vignette: Compact Ops Cards & Burst Controls
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Purpose: Design a compact, information-dense set of operational ‘vignette’ cards for Dedicated GPU fleets that surface pool health, autoscaling status, cost impact, and an inline burst control. These cards are intended for a horizontal compact strip used on the Fleet Overview and for expansion into a lightweight inspector panel.

Scope: low- to mid-fidelity mockups + interactive prototype for engineering handoff. Must include: 1) compact health sparkline + thermal indicator, 2) autoscale state (policy name + active targets), 3) burst control with hysteresis preview and safety guardrails, 4) per-card cost delta estimate and quick actions (force-burst, pause-autoscale, inspect-logs).

Users: platform operators, SREs, and product engineers who need quick triage and controlled overrides without leaving the Fleet Overview.

Constraints/assumptions: cards need to be screen-reader friendly and keyboard-accessible, fit 3–5 cards per row at 1366px width, and avoid heavy telemetry polling (use sampled telemetry + on-demand refresh). The burst control must respect RBAC; non-admins see an explainers and request-flow.

Success metrics: adoption in Fleet Overview, reduced mean time to remediation for burst incidents, and no measurable increase in API request volume from the console telemetry pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Design files (Figma) include: compact card states (normal, degraded, critical), expanded inspector state, and burst-dialog flows.
Prototype demonstrates burst slider with hysteresis preview and simulated latency/cost curves.
Accessibility checklist completed: ARIA labels for interactive controls, contrast ratios verified, keyboard tab order defined.
Developer-facing spec includes tokenized UI colors, spacing scale, component variants, and analytics event list.
PM and Eng sign-off on default burst hysteresis and RBAC gating behavior.
comments: 2025-03-01 - Kickoff: aligned with PM on scope; Rafael to confirm necessary telemetry fields with Eng infra team (ENG-4124 flagged as dependency).
2025-03-04 - Sketches: created three layout modes (stacked, strip, mosaic). PM prefers strip for list density; ops asked for quick-action affordances.

2025-03-06 - Usability test (5 participants): operators favored a single-click burst toggle but wanted a short confirmation microcopy to avoid accidental bursts. Observed confusion around cost delta units—changed to daily/hourly estimate options.

2025-03-08 - Engineering sync: agreed to use sampled telemetry and a refresh button to avoid rate limits. Eng requests payload schema and event names; added to attachments. Rafael to surface RBAC API shape.
2025-03-10 - Accessibility pass: voiceover reads card title + status; need to add aria-live for critical state transitions. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-03-12 - Design review: consolidated to two variants (compact strip + expanded inspector). Minor color adjustments and reduced iconography to improve scanability. Rafael asked for final tokens by 2025-03-14 for CSS extraction.
decisions: Use compact horizontal vignette cards as primary Fleet Overview element (3 cards per row at default width).
Burst control will be a two-stage interaction: slide to propose + confirm modal summarizing cost/latency impact. Default hysteresis preview set to 3 minutes (configurable per-pool).
Per-card cost estimate shows 1h and 24h deltas; values are estimates derived from moving-average throughput, not exact billing.
Non-admins see a request-flow UI for burst: request -> approval event in Ops channel; admins see direct controls.
review_feedback: Maya Patel (PM): Add a lightweight cost tooltip that explains assumptions and links to pricing docs.
Jun Park (Eng): Ensure telemetry hook 'fleet.vignette.burst_propose' and 'fleet.vignette.burst_confirm' exist; add server-side validation for hysteresis limits.
Liam O'Connor (Security): Burst override must be audited; include an audit-event ID in the success response and a link to the audit details.
Accessibility Reviewer: Provide high-contrast critical state variant and announce state changes via aria-live polite for non-blocking info, assertive for critical.
next_steps: Incorporate review feedback into Figma and produce v0.3 annotations (due 2025-03-14).
Handoff package: tokenized color/spacing, SVG icons, and analytics event list to Eng (Rafael) by 2025-03-16.
Add an A/B test plan to measure whether compact vignette reduces time-to-first-action vs existing Fleet Overview (PM to create experiment ticket).
Prepare short runbook copy for burst misuse scenarios and place into the inspector 'Help' panel.
